input: This capital appraisal considers a proposed warehouse extension and returns a net present value of $280k. The installed cost of the extension is $579k, and the expected net saving is estimated at $128k per year for 10 years. When the savings are discounted at 8%, they are found to have a present value of $859k, and the excess of that present value over the installed cost represents a net present value of $280k. A positive net present value indicates that the project returns more than the discount rate that was used to appraise it. It is important to note that the appraisal is expressed in today's money: the discounting process converts each year's saving into the sum that, if it were held now, would be equivalent to it, and the net figure is what remains after the cost of the extension has been charged against the converted savings. Over the 10 years, the saving is assumed to be held at $128k per year, and the result is sensitive to this assumption, in that a saving below the estimate would reduce the present value of $859k towards the installed cost and narrow the margin accordingly. Furthermore, the savings are vendor and utility estimates, and no saving has yet been measured on a comparable installation. The margin is therefore provisional in a specific sense: it depends on figures that have been supplied by the parties who would sell or supply the works, and it is the first years of operation, when metered savings can be compared with the estimate, that would confirm or remove it.
